scenes.heading: Negative and fractional indices
scenes.say: You know that two cubed is eight. But what could two to the power of negative three mean? Or eight to the power of two thirds? By the end of this video, both will make perfect sense.
scenes.caption: You know that 2³ = 8. But what could 2⁻³ mean? Or 8^(2/3)? By the end of this video, both will make perfect sense.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Walking down a staircase: each step down, divide by 2
scenes.breaks: A staircase has whole steps only, but an index can be any number — and 2ˣ always stays positive.
scenes.say: Picture the powers of two as a staircase. Eight, four, two, one. Every step down, you divide by two. Keep going past two to the zero, and you get a half, a quarter, an eighth. A negative index just means keep dividing. The numbers get small, but they never go negative.

scenes.heading: Negative index: one over
scenes.say: A negative index means one over. a to the negative n equals one over a to the n. So three to the negative two is one ninth, not negative nine. For a fraction, just flip it: two thirds to the negative two is three halves squared.
scenes.caption: a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ. So 3⁻² = 1/9, not −9. For a fraction, flip it: (2/3)⁻² = (3/2)².

scenes.heading: Fractional index: root, then power
scenes.say: A fractional index means a root. The bottom number is the root and the top number is the power. Twenty-seven to the power of two thirds: cube root of twenty-seven is three, then three squared is nine. Take the root first so the numbers stay small.
scenes.caption: The bottom number is the root and the top number is the power. 27^(2/3): ∛27 = 3, then 3² = 9. Take the root first so the numbers stay small.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Evaluate (8/27)^(−2/3).
scenes.say: Evaluate eight twenty-sevenths to the power of negative two thirds. The minus sign says flip: twenty-seven eighths. The three says cube root: three halves. The two says square: nine quarters.
scenes.caption: Evaluate (8/27)^(−2/3). The minus sign says flip: 27/8. The 3 says cube root: 3/2. The 2 says square: 9/4.

scenes.heading: For a^(−m/n)
scenes.say: Whenever you see a negative fractional index, do three jobs: flip, root, power. Then make sure your final answer has only positive indices.

scenes.heading: Simplifying
scenes.question: Simplify (16x⁸y⁻⁴)^(3/4) with positive indices.
scenes.say: Now with pronumerals. Raise every factor to the power three quarters. Sixteen to the three quarters is two cubed, eight. For x and y, multiply the indices: x to the six, y to the negative three. Move y below the line: eight x to the six over y cubed.
scenes.caption: Raise every factor to the power ¾. 16^(3/4) = 2³ = 8. Multiply the indices: x⁶ and y⁻³. Move y below the line: 8x⁶/y³.

points: A negative index never makes it negative
scenes.say: Quick recap. A negative index means flip, and it never makes the answer negative. A fractional index is a root. For m over n, take the root first, then the power. Now try the practice questions!
